title: U.S. House · Hawaii's 1st District
area: Urban Honolulu, on the island of Oahu.

context.text: Incumbent Ed Case (D) won the August 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 60% of the vote over state Sen. Jarrett Keohokalole. Adriel Lam ran unopposed for the Republican nomination, Jordan Conley ran unopposed for the Green nomination, and Nathan Berning ran unopposed in the nonpartisan primary.

candidates.name: Ed Case

summary.text: Ed Case is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election. He previously represented Hawaii's 2nd District from 2002 to 2007 and served in the Hawaii House of Representatives, and is running on his seniority and record in Congress, including his handling of COVID-19, Red Hill, and the Maui wildfires.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Williams College and a law degree from the University of California, San Francisco.
Worked as an attorney with the law firms Carlsmith Ball and Bays Lung Rose & Holma, and as senior vice president and chief legal officer of Outrigger Hotels.
Served in the Hawaii House of Representatives, District 23 (1994-2002), and previously represented Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District (2002-2007).

priorities.text: Continuing to build seniority in Congress; says re-election would move him to the top 25% of House seniority and let him continue on the Appropriations Committee.
The cost of living, which he calls his top priority, citing housing, food, gas, and childcare costs.
Points to his record responding to COVID-19, the Red Hill fuel contamination crisis, and the Maui wildfires.

positions.summary: Supports protecting and improving the Affordable Care Act and has voted for extending enhanced ACA premium tax credits, which he says have made coverage more affordable for tens of thousands of Hawai'i residents.
positions.quote: I am committed to achieving access to affordable, quality health care for all Americans.

positions.summary: Supported the Inflation Reduction Act's climate investments, opposed the 2025 reconciliation law's rollback of IRA clean-energy funding, and has introduced legislation to expand clean-energy resilience for Hawai'i's isolated communities.
positions.quote: I supported the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which was our nation’s largest-ever investment in the fight against climate change.

positions.summary: Says broad tariffs have raised the cost of living and harmed Hawai'i businesses and families, and has cosponsored bills to limit the president's unilateral tariff authority.
positions.quote: I believe tariffs should be used more cautiously and in ways that protect, not harm, American families and industries, and I am committed to working with my colleagues in Congress to restore the necessary checks and balances over trade policy and undo the harm placed on everyday Americans.

record.text: Serves on the House Appropriations Committee in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Adriel Lam

summary.text: Adriel Lam is the Republican nominee. He is a nearly 24-year U.S. Army veteran whose family has lived in Hawaii for several generations, running on government accountability, election security, and Hawaii's strategic role in the Pacific.

background.text: Describes his family's history in Hawaii spanning generations, including a great-grandfather who arrived in 1872 and a grandfather who worked at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard during the 1941 attack.
Served nearly 24 years of active-duty service in the U.S. Army, including leading combat units and enterprise-wide efforts with inter-agency and international partners.

priorities.text: Hawaii's strategic role as a military and economic gateway to the Pacific.
Election security, including support for voter photo ID requirements.
Names as his top priority passing a $5,000 dividend for every U.S. citizen, and says Congress should repeal or reform the Jones Act to lower shipping costs to Hawaii.

candidates.researchNotes: Lam's statements come from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and a Honolulu Star-Advertiser candidate questionnaire (Oct. 9, 2026). His website (lam4aloha.com) has a short statement on Hawaii's strategic role and links to profiles but no issue pages. Nothing found on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, or tariffs.

statements.quote: Congress should focus on investing in the improvements and maintenance of our national infrastructure. Long-term climate prognostications contribute little to necessary mitigations and improvements to current weather and storm impacts.
statements.context: Answer to a Honolulu Star-Advertiser candidate questionnaire, Oct. 9, 2026

candidates.name: Jordan Conley

summary.text: Jordan Conley is the Green Party nominee. He is a personal trainer and coach who founded the nonprofit Hapa Mana in 2016, running on universal healthcare, a housing-first approach to homelessness, and opposition to U.S. military engagement abroad.

background.text: Has worked as a personal trainer, coach, and teacher for 16 years, and previously as a bartender and server.
Founded the nonprofit Hapa Mana in 2016, which used sports and educational enrichment to integrate communities across income lines, before COVID-19 disruptions ended in-person programming.

priorities.text: Universal healthcare, which he says he would pursue nationally and, if that fails, at the state level in Hawaii.
A "housing first" program to address homelessness, funded through proposed taxes on empty homes and visitors.
Opposition to U.S. military intervention and foreign occupation.

positions.summary: Says universal healthcare is his number-one issue and he would push for a national vote on it, or pursue it at the state level if that fails.
positions.quote: I will try to force a vote on national universal health care ASAP.

positions.summary: In a Star-Advertiser questionnaire, answering a question about Social Security funding, he wrote 'Tax the rich' and cited historical top tax rates.
In a Star-Advertiser questionnaire he said a cap on rent could be put in place and that he favors government-built or purchased apartments rented at no profit.
positions.quote: We could also put a cap on rent.

candidates.researchNotes: Conley's own survey statements include broader political characterizations of major-party donors and U.S. foreign policy; those framing choices are his own words, quoted where used, and are not adopted as this guide's characterization. Additional positions come from his Honolulu Star-Advertiser questionnaire; his campaign site (jordanforhawaii.com) was not fetched.

statements.quote: We should listen to scientists which I am no one. Planting more trees will help pull carbon out of the air. I am sure that is not enough.
statements.context: Answer to a Honolulu Star-Advertiser candidate questionnaire

candidates.name: Nathan Berning

summary.text: Nathan Berning is a nonpartisan candidate who ran unopposed in the nonpartisan primary, receiving 877 votes.

priorities.text: Names 'right-to-keep' legislation as his top policy priority: economic support such as housing, food, utilities and transportation for pregnant women.
Campaign website lists five priorities: cost of living and housing, the Right to Keep, local jobs and small business, water, land and island resilience, and independent and accountable government.

positions.summary: His campaign website says he opposes abortion and that no mother should be pushed toward abortion by poverty; in an Oct. 2026 Civil Beat interview he also said he has always been pro-choice and argued the government should help women facing financial hardship.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions come from his campaign website (berningforcongress.com) and a Honolulu Civil Beat interview (Oct. 2026). He has not completed Ballotpedia's survey. Civil Beat reports he lives outside Hawaii; the campaign site describes his priorities in general terms and states a stance only on abortion; its other priority text is general.
